intro: These questions are kept out of the Learn and Exam views because neither the slides nor the TA's pen marks settle the answer. Each one shows the original slide, so you can read the full question without going back to the deck, along with any pen mark and what makes it uncertain.

groups.title: Conflicting keys
groups.desc: The slide's key disagrees with the slide's own figure or working.

items.q: Looking at Figure 4 (distance between real and inferred user home city, for INCORRECT inferences only), which dataset shows the largest share of its incorrect inferences falling within 50 km of the true city?
options: All three datasets are statistically indistinguishable
items.mark: The TA ticked A and drew a line at 50 km on the inset.
items.note: In the inset of Fig. 4, the Foursquare curve (solid green) is highest at 50 km, at about 0.46; Google+ and Twitter are both near 0.25. That matches option B, not the printed key A. No curve reaches 0.87 at 50 km.

groups.title: No key on the slide
groups.desc: The slide printed no answer, and more than one option can be defended.

items.mark: Q49 is top left. No pen mark on it.

items.q: Collecting personal details from Facebook to launch a phishing attack is an example of:
items.note: The TA's own option notes call "social surfing" a non-standard term, yet no other option fits.
items.mark: Q59 is bottom left. No pen mark on it.

items.q: Which command counts all documents in MongoDB?
items.note: A and B both worked in the old mongo shell and are both deprecated; the current command is db.users.countDocuments({}).

items.q: Which groups correctly identify police departments that were among the earliest Twitter/X adopters in their countries? 1. USA: NYPD, Boston PD · 2. UK: West Midlands Police · 3. India: Delhi Traffic, Bangalore Traffic Police
items.mark: Q28 is at the top. The TA ticked and boxed D, "2 only".

items.q: What is the status of the official X API's standalone free tier?
options: Available with 10,000 free reads a month
Discontinued; new developers start on pay-per-use from 2025
items.note: B is the intended idea, but X made pay-per-use the default on 6 Feb 2026, not 2025.
items.mark: Q1 is at the top. The TA ticked B.

items.q: What trial credit does TwitterAPI.io give new accounts?
items.note: TwitterAPI.io's blog says $1 and about 6,000 calls; its homepage and several listings say $0.10.
items.mark: Q3 is on the left. The TA ticked A, which disagrees with what TwitterAPI.io itself publishes.

items.q: Which inference is correct?
options: The percentage follows a Pareto distribution
It does not follow a Pareto distribution
items.mark: Q6 is at the bottom. The TA struck through the first three options; it is unclear which are meant as correct.

items.where: Last class: Gmail "To" field with recipient chips
items.q: This is an example of the ideas proposed by Facemail from MIT.
items.mark: Q3 is at the top. No clear pen mark.

items.q: Look at Figure 1 (cumulative distribution of the number of mayorships, tips and dones per user). "Majority of the users on Foursquare do not contribute to the Mayorships, Tips or Dones." This statement is:
items.mark: The TA struck through part of the statement and through "True"; it is unclear whether that means False.
items.note: The figure only covers users who have at least one mayorship, tip or done, so it cannot show how many contribute nothing.

items.where: Last class: Whisper response time of replies
items.q: Observe the graph regarding replies on Whisper. "If a whisper does not get attention shortly after posting, it is unlikely to get attention later." This statement is:
items.mark: There is a stroke beside "False", but the TA also wrote "Whisper 94% 1 day".
items.note: The lecture states this exact conclusion, and about 94% of replies arrive within a day, which supports True.

items.q: A second version of "Calculate the GlobalEngagement for Aditya" lists the options 0.1, 0.05 and 10.
items.mark: 0.1 is highlighted on the slide, next to the TA's note "What to calculate? Q not [clear]".
items.note: The question text does not say which quantity this version wants. (1,000 favourites ÷ 10,000 statuses = 0.1 is one reading.) The first version, 10.96, is in the Last class set.

items.q: Which are goals of a phishing attack? (multi-select)
items.mark: The TA ticked A and B only.
items.note: The TA marked only personal and financial information, although identity theft and attacking your contacts are also common phishing goals.

items.q: Degrees of separation have reduced on social media due to:
items.mark: The TA drew a bracket beside A–C and a stroke at D; it is unclear which is meant.

items.q: Which method(s) measured similarity between two consecutive usernames?
items.mark: The TA bracketed the question and wrote "Check the weekly content".

items.q: Social media constitutes:
items.note: No "all of the above" option was printed.

items.q: In which format does an API usually return its response?
Which attributes can be inferred from data collected via X (formerly Twitter)?
options: Number of likes of the Tweet
Number of times the Tweet has been viewed
Unique identifier of the Tweet's author
items.note: X returns like and view counts and the author ID, so A, B and C all look right, but the slide does not say whether more than one may be chosen.

items.q: Which processes can be used to obtain annotated posts while determining their legitimacy?
options: A group of friends annotating posts
items.note: All three are used to label posts in the course (friends in early studies, Mechanical Turk, fact-checkers), pointing to D, but no key is given.

items.q: Which is the correct syntax for labeling the legend of a scatter plot in Highcharts?
items.note: In the python-highcharts library the third argument of add_data_set is the series name, so both A (name=…) and B (positional) set the legend label.

items.q: What is the difference between Pearson and Spearman rank correlation?
options: Pearson assesses linear relationships; Spearman evaluates monotonic relationships
Spearman is always between -1 and 1, while Pearson can fall outside this range
Spearman uses squared rank differences; Pearson is based on the product of z-scores
items.note: A and C are both true and B is false, so "All of the above" is wrong, yet the question expects a single option.

items.q: Which features can be used for profile linking between Facebook and X for a boy called Arjun?
options: Similarity between people Arjun follows on both platforms
Similarity between people who follow Arjun on both platforms
items.note: All four can serve as linking features; the slide does not say how many to pick.

items.q: Which statements are correct about the Web of Trust score?
options: It outputs the reputation of an input website
Domain Age can be used as a feature
Domain Owner can be used as a feature
items.note: The lecture names the WOT reputation score but the slides do not list which features it uses.

items.q: Which of the following is/are location-based services?
items.note: Foursquare, Ola, Yelp and Uber all depend on location; whether ride-hailing apps count as "location-based services" in the course is not stated.

items.q: Which methods were used to gather information across India in the report?
items.note: The slide does not say which report this refers to.

items.q: Which method resulted in the largest number of respondents across India?
items.note: The slide does not say which report this refers to.

items.q: What is the purpose of k-anonymity, as discussed in the lecture?
items.note: k-anonymity protects people from re-identification while keeping the data useful; A and B each state half of that.

items.q: Latanya Sweeney's experiments aimed to:
options: Re-identify individuals from Match.com using Facebook profiles
Identify individuals walking on a campus with Facebook data
Predict social security numbers from public data
Study behaviors of individuals aged 14-18 on Instagram
items.note: None of the options describes Sweeney's best-known study (re-identifying a governor's medical records via a voter list). B and C describe work by Acquisti and colleagues.

items.q: What is the output of pd.Series(['A','B','C'], index=[1, 2, 3])?
options: None of the above 1 A 2 B 3 C dtype: object
items.note: The options were garbled when the slide was made, so the printed series layout cannot be read reliably.

items.q: What are the outcomes of publicizing police interactions on X (formerly Twitter)?
options: Appreciation of the Police by the Public
items.note: All three are plausible outcomes; the slide gives no key.

items.q: Which social media campaign to create trust in the police backfired, as discussed in the lectures?
items.note: #myNYPD (2014) is the well-known backfire; #myLAPD drew similar criticism soon after, so A alone may not be what is wanted.

items.q: Communication of the police with citizens on social media is ………
items.note: The lecture discusses both formal and informal tones in police posts; the expected answer is not clear.

items.q: Students of the PSOSM course are divided into groups by Indian state. This is best achieved using:
items.note: Grouping students by a known attribute (their state) needs no clustering, so "None of the above" may be intended rather than k-means.

items.q: Which are the most widely used formats to represent node-edge graphs on computers?
items.note: Adjacency matrices, edge-list CSVs and GraphML are all common; the slide does not say how many to pick.

items.q: Which measures of behavior can be studied when analyzing police–citizen communication on social media?
items.note: All four appear in police–citizen communication studies; no key is given.

items.q: According to the study, which users were most likely to reciprocate links from spammers?
items.note: The link-farming study's exact finding on which users reciprocate is not on the slides.

items.q: According to the study, which users usually engaged in Link Farming?
options: People talking about Business, Internet Marketing, Money etc.
People promoting their own business or content
Equally distributed among random Twitter users
items.note: The study found link farmers are mainly "social capitalists" promoting themselves; A and B both partly describe them.

Giving you the opportunity to cancel your post within a timeframe
Making sure your posts are not perceived as negative

items.q: Table orders(order_id PK, customer_id, total_amount, order_date, status). The question sentence is missing; only the four queries survive.
options: ... WHERE customer_id = 1001 AND status='Completed' ORDER BY order_date DESC LIMIT 10;
... WHERE customer_id=1001 ORDER BY order_id DESC LIMIT 10;
... WHERE status='Completed' ORDER BY order_date ASC LIMIT 10;
... WHERE customer_id=1001 ORDER BY total_amount DESC;
items.note: If the question asks for customer 1001's ten most recent completed orders, A is right.
items.mark: Q40 is bottom right. The slide has an empty box where the question should be.

items.note: No options were printed. The slide's answer is "only ii is correct".
